overall: One continuous, conversational read by someone who knows Texas freight routes. Begin with close curiosity at the open cab, build slightly as the road appears, then drop the reported mileage to a quieter factual register. Lift only enough to show the human role McLane describes. The filing limit is the quietest line. End lower and firmer than the middle, leaving the comparison unresolved without trailer gravity. Keep a normal speaking pace and natural breaths; the editor creates any extended silence. Say Aurora as uh-ROAR-uh, Dallas as DALL-us, Houston as HYOO-stun, and McLane as mick-LANE. Read only the locked text, with no spoken directions or performed accent.
editor_note: Pause values are editorial beats only. Synthesis is one continuous passage; do not instruct the reader to hold gaps. If a line exceeds its scene, trim the script through the director and resync this file. Never stretch audio.

lines.text: Aurora offered attendees a seat beside an empty wheel.
lines.intent: Let the passenger side of the cab open the question in a personal, physical way. Keep the empty wheel plain and observed.
lines.energy: five of ten, close curiosity; no headline rise
lines.risk: Aurora needs a natural three-syllable pronunciation. Do not turn the empty seat into a claim that a ride occurred.

lines.text: The ride was offered on one segment of its Dallas to Houston freight route.
lines.intent: Set the geographic scope carefully. The offer is on one segment, and the longer route gives context only.
lines.energy: six of ten, a modest lift as the road extends
lines.risk: This is the longest geographic sentence. Keep Dallas to Houston connected at normal speed; if it overruns, ask the director for a shorter line.

lines.text: The offer describes a commercial route with nobody behind the wheel.
lines.intent: Bring the idea into a working freight lane while holding the distinction between a described offer and a documented trip.
lines.energy: six and a half of ten, a brief forward push
lines.risk: Do not imply that attendees actually rode or that this describes the full corridor.

lines.text: Aurora says its trucks have logged over 500,000 driverless miles.
lines.intent: Land the reported distance as a company statement. Give the number room to register without swelling.
lines.energy: three and a half of ten, a deliberate drop and the first restrained fact
lines.risk: Say five hundred thousand clearly. Preserve Aurora says; the figure is cumulative and self-reported.

lines.text: McLane says its drivers can focus on their expertise and customer service.
lines.intent: Turn toward the worker and the role McLane describes, with practical warmth and no triumphant tone.
lines.energy: five of ten, a human-scale recovery from the number
lines.risk: Preserve McLane says. Do not suggest any specific driver was reassigned or a job outcome occurred.

lines.text: The filing offers a ride. It does not confirm anyone boarded.
lines.intent: Set the offered card against the missing confirmation. Let the second sentence settle without a dramatic hold.
lines.energy: two and a half of ten, the quietest and most certain line
lines.risk: Keep offers and does not confirm distinct. No completed passenger ride appears in the reviewed filing.

lines.text: Those miles are Aurora's count. They don't compare safety with human drivers.
lines.intent: Separate reported distance from the safety comparison the source does not provide. Connect the two sentences as one thought.
lines.energy: four of ten on the mileage clause, easing to three on the comparison limit
lines.risk: Do not suggest the mileage itself proves a safety result. If this sentence runs long, ask the director to trim words; never compress the audio.

lines.text: A passenger could see the empty seat. A short ride can't answer for every mile.
lines.intent: Return to the opening seat and answer the question: a passenger can observe the missing driver, while a short segment leaves the wider claim open.
lines.energy: three and a half of ten, then settle to three at the final word
lines.risk: Could is hypothetical. Give the last clause a plain final landing, without an upward promo cadence.
